questions.q: What does Ariely call the number one factor in motivation?
a: A sense of meaning
A high salary
Public status
Frequent recognition
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls meaning the number one factor, more important than money or status.

questions.q: What did the origami experiment show?
a: People valued their own work more after putting in effort
Clear instructions produced more valuable origami
Groups produced better origami than individuals
People preferred origami made by experts
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the origami study, where the poorly guided group valued their own work more.

questions.q: What happened to Intel workers after receiving a cash bonus?
a: Productivity fell below normal once the money was paid
They kept improving for weeks afterward
They asked for even larger bonuses
They shared the money with colleagues
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes Intel workers whose productivity dropped below normal after a cash bonus.

questions.q: Which group performed best in Ariely's follow-up comparison?
a: The group that received a compliment
The group that received a cash bonus
The group that received free pizza
The group that received extra time off
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the compliment group outperformed the pizza group throughout the week.

questions.q: What does Ariely mean by effort engenders meaning?
a: The more work you put in, the more meaningful it seems
Effort should be minimized to stay motivated
Meaningful work always requires less effort
Only paid effort feels worthwhile
questions.why: Lesson 2 says effort creates meaning, partly because of the sunk cost fallacy.
